hero.tagline: Where we lead, where we lag, and what to build next.
hero.subtitle: A sample analysis of Acme Outreach against two fictional platforms, included only to demonstrate the report format.

tldr.sub: What's actually true once you read the matrix in Section 04.
paragraphs: Acme Outreach is not sitting in the middle of Brandly and Bidwise. It looks like Brandly on the surface (content, workflows, brand, approvals) and runs like Bidwise underneath, with scale, reliability, and governance baked in. But it doesn't yet own the features customers actually buy from either platform.

It owns the foundation they sit on: reproducibility, live tracking, approval gates, encrypted credentials, tenant isolation. These are the bones; the muscle on top is the work for the next two quarters.

capabilities.name: Brand voice & guidelines
capabilities.reality: We can store voice, look, and pillars. We can't yet enforce them at generation time.

capabilities.name: One-click brand from a URL
capabilities.reality: Brandly scrapes a company website and builds the brand profile. We start blank.

capabilities.name: AI deliverability score
capabilities.reality: Brandly grades messages for deliverability before send. We don't score yet.

capabilities.name: Bulk message packs
capabilities.reality: One brief to many assets. Brandly ships templates; we run it manually.

capabilities.name: Message generation at scale
capabilities.reality: Both Brandly and we generate at volume; Bidwise is not a content tool.

capabilities.name: Bid optimization
capabilities.reality: Bidwise has years of ML bidding. Neither Brandly nor we play here.

capabilities.name: Budget pacing
capabilities.reality: Bidwise paces spend across channels live. We can cap, not pace.

capabilities.name: Channel breadth
capabilities.reality: Bidwise integrates 50+ channels. We integrate the few our buyers use.

capabilities.name: Attribution & measurement
capabilities.reality: Bidwise owns this; Brandly and we report at the campaign level only.

capabilities.name: Live run tracking
capabilities.reality: Watch every step as it happens, resumes cleanly across devices. Ours alone.

capabilities.name: Human approval gates
capabilities.reality: Approve, reject, or rewrite a step mid-run with a recorded decision.

capabilities.name: Reproducible playbooks
capabilities.reality: Re-run next month, get an identical result. Neither competitor guarantees this.

capabilities.name: Multi-tenant isolation
capabilities.reality: Data, spend, and limits walled off per customer from day one.

capabilities.name: Connector auto-recovery
capabilities.reality: Connectors detect outages, hold, probe, and resume with no operator.

ahead.sub: Engineering moats Brandly and Bidwise don't trivially copy. Defend these; they're the wedge for enterprise sales.

items.title: Reproducible playbooks
items.body: Re-run the same playbook next month and get an identical result. Neither Brandly nor Bidwise offers this guarantee.

items.title: Live run tracking
items.body: Watch every step as it happens. Refresh, drop network, switch devices — the view resumes cleanly.

items.title: Human approval gates
items.body: A reviewer can approve, reject, or rewrite a step mid-run. The workflow pauses, the decision is recorded, execution resumes.

items.title: Connector reliability
items.body: When a vendor goes down or a credential expires, our connectors detect, hold, probe for recovery, and resume — with no operator intervention.

items.title: Enterprise-grade isolation
items.body: Every customer's data, spend, and limits walled off from day one. No retrofitting needed for compliance.

closeable.sub: Each gap maps to existing schema or services. Six items, all shippable inside a quarter.

items.title: AI deliverability score
items.desc: A scorer that grades messages against deliverability guidelines before send

items.title: One-click brand from URL
items.desc: Scrape a company website and auto-fill brand voice, audience, and knowledge base

items.title: Bulk message-pack template
items.desc: One brief in → email, social, and follow-up sequence out, in one run

items.title: Playbook comparison dashboard
items.desc: Side-by-side view of cost, completion rate, and outcomes across playbooks

items.title: Finish connector refresh
items.desc: The last piece of plumbing to keep connected vendor tools auto-updated

items.title: UTM auto-tagging
items.desc: Stamp every output with the right tracking parameters automatically

decisions.sub: Not engineering tasks. These get decided in a leadership room, not a sprint.

items.title: Bidding
items.body: Do we play in bid optimization at all? Bidwise has years of ML bidding behind their engine. We'd be several engineers deep before we caught up.

items.title: Channels
items.body: Match Bidwise's 50+ channel coverage, or pick the few our buyers actually use? This is a partnerships problem, not a coding one.

items.title: SOC 2
items.body: When does SOC 2 stop being optional? The trigger is usually the first enterprise procurement call.

items.title: In-product chat
items.body: Do we build chat at all, or assume buyers use a general assistant alongside us? Only the brand-aware version is worth building.

positioning.sub: The one paragraph to keep in your head after closing this doc.
paragraphs: Acme Outreach is not sitting between Brandly and Bidwise. It is the execution platform underneath them that neither one offers: live tracking, multi-tenant from day one, encrypted credentials per customer, human approval gates, and reproducible playbooks.
Brandly sits above a platform like this and bundles a polished content interface on top. Bidwise sits beside it and sells media buying. The real position:
positioning.pullquote: Brandly's content intelligence on Bidwise's enterprise reliability, with an open connector model.
positioning.closing: Three things stand between us and saying that out loud: brand-from-URL, a deliverability score, and bulk message packs before we can stand next to Brandly. On Bidwise's side, the call isn't engineering — it's whether we want to play in bidding at all.
